7.0.0.en: "After these things," that is, after the miracle of feeding the crowds and the lengthy discourse about "His body and blood," Christ stayed for a time in Galilee, keeping away from Judaea, the southern region, because of the envy of the Jews and their complaint against Christ who had broken the Sabbath, and they sought to kill Him for this reason.

7.0.1.en: St. John Chrysostom says: "Christ teaches us here an important principle, which is that keeping away from danger and fleeing from persecutors, wherever necessity requires it, is a kind of wisdom and prudence, for confrontation is in many cases not necessary" ...

7.0.2.en: And Christ here, God forbid, was not afraid, for He knew that He would give Himself up, but there is a time for everything.

7.1.0.en: "The feast of tabernacles": one of the three great feasts of the Jews. The duration of the feast was 8 days, and its place was Jerusalem, and it is called the season of harvest, and this feast was imposed on Israel by God (Ex 23:16) for the following spiritual meanings:

7.1.1.en: (1) A memorial of sojourning: all leave their homes and dwell under booths on the rooftops or on the roads, that God may remind them of the forty years they spent in the wilderness, and then how God gave them this land as an inheritance.

7.1.2.en: (2) Thanksgiving and joy: the harvest begins with the first of the feasts, the Passover, but is completed at the time of the feast of tabernacles, so there is thanksgiving and joy for the blessings of the whole year.

7.1.3.en: My beloved God ... make me always remember that I am here in a time of sojourning, wandering, but my true and lasting rest is with You there where the true, abiding inheritance is, so do not let anything distract me from You and from it, and help me to spend my sojourning in peace ...

7.2.0.en: "His brethren": St. Matthew mentioned them (13:55), and they are James, Joses, Simon and Judas; they are brothers of Christ, but not from the holy Virgin St. Mary, for cousins on the mother's or father's side are called brothers in the region of the Levant, as Abraham and Lot were anciently called brothers, although Abraham was his uncle.

7.2.1.en: What these brothers said to Christ, in brief, is: you must go where the crowds and the throng are at the feast of tabernacles, to do your miracles there, so that everyone believes in you, instead of doing these wonders here in the small villages where no one knows you. But St. John reveals to us a secret that clarifies the motive for this advice, and this secret is (v. 5): that His brethren did not believe in Him. Consequently, they wanted Christ to go to Jerusalem, so that the priests and scribes might examine Him to know whether He is the Christ or not.

7.3.0.en: "My time is not yet come": it bears two meanings; the first is what concerns the time of His crucifixion and redemption and offering Himself as a sacrifice for the world. The second: I will go up, but not now. For going up openly amid a state of expectation would stir the envy of the leaders, and they would seek Him to death before the appointed time, which God Himself determined. And this meaning agrees with the context of the events in the same chapter (vv. 10, 14) in His going up to Jerusalem concealing Himself, and then His speaking in the temple.

7.3.1.en: "Your time is alway ready": that is, you can go to the feast at any time.

7.4.0.en: The Lord here points to the reason for the Jews' hatred and their not accepting Him, which is that the world as a whole, because of the sin of self-love, does not accept reproof, but is ready even to kill anyone who reproves it, for he who loves darkness hates the light. When Christ exposed their sins to them, they demanded His destruction, instead of listening to Him and repenting of them.

7.4.1.en: Would that our hearts were humbled and confessed their sins, and that we listened to Your voice, O Savior, so that we reprove ourselves, instead of venturing, in many cases, to throw the blame on You for the discipline that we ourselves deserve.

7.5.0.en: The Lord Christ completes His discourse to His brethren about their going with the crowds going up to Jerusalem, withdrawing from going with them, presenting what He had said before in (v. 6) about the appointed time for His going; and we may infer from the comparison with (v. 14) that He stayed in Galilee about 4 days, until the middle of the feast, before He appeared in Jerusalem.

7.6.s.en: (2) Christ's going up to Jerusalem and His teaching in the temple

7.6.0.en: The Lord Christ went up secretly to Jerusalem, which was an act of the utmost wisdom. Had He gone up with the crowds, they would have proclaimed Him king, as happened at His last visit to Jerusalem, and this is contrary to the plan He intended, especially since His hour had not yet come.

7.6.1.en: May we learn in our prayers to wait for God's answer at the time He sees fit, for God has plans for our lives that we cannot reach; rather, let us know that to everything under heaven there is a season.

7.6.2.en: St. John also depicts the state of the Jews who were watching for Christ's appearing at the first days of the feast, with the question, "Where is he?", which carries in its meaning contempt and malice more than longing expectation. This reveals to us that the waiting had something of lying in ambush, and it confirms Christ's wisdom in choosing the right time to go.

7.7.0.en: Opinions clashed about the person of Christ, for some said "He is a good man," that is, upright and without fault; and the others said that "he deceiveth the people," that is, misleads them. The saints agree that the other group were the envious among the supporters of the scribes and Pharisees, whom Christ had reproved. Yet no one dared to speak of it openly, but most of the talk was in small groups and in secret, because of fear of the leaders and rulers of the Jews (the priests and the Pharisees).

7.8.0.en: That is, after four days, Christ declared Himself, and appeared in the temple with authority, and even began to teach the crowds. St. Matthew describes that His appearing thus took the leaders by surprise, and despite their fury at Him they were afraid to oppose Him, "lest there be an uproar among the people" (Mt 26:5); see also (Mt 21:46).

7.8.1.en: The reaction of the Jews was astonishment at the loftiness, beauty and precision of the teaching, expressing this astonishment by saying that Christ was not known to be one of the disciples of the Jewish scholars, so how then does He know the Scriptures, that is, the prophecies and the Law, in all their details?

7.9.0.en: This scene is repeated more than once, whether murmuring, or wonder, or whispering, which the Lord Christ read on faces, or knew by His divinity, even without anyone putting a direct question to Him. And as the Lord Christ knew what was in their minds about His origin and His teaching according to their bodily view ... He answered what was perplexing them: that the source of all this is the Father who sent Him into the world. And although the Father and the Son are one, Christ knew well that if He said that He was the source of the teaching, the Jews would not accept it, so He attributed it to the Father, as He had said before: "The Father Himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me" (ch. 5:37).

7.10.0.en: Christ adds in His discourse the means of verifying the truth of the teaching which the Jews hear; the means here is not discipleship under the hands of the Jewish teachers, but the only means here is that man be in accord with God's will, doing it and submitting to it in his life, for this way alone leads man to the knowledge of the truth, and none can discern the voice of God except one who fulfills His will and does it.

7.11.0.en: The Lord adds here and affirms His connection to the Source, for He does not seek glory for Himself as the Pharisees do, and this is a proof of the truth and righteousness of His word.

7.11.1.en: My beloved God ... You taught us what self-emptying is, You who are the Owner of all glory and honor, and even took the form of a servant, attributing everything to the Father, though You are heavenly to Him ... But I still steal Your glory and boast of everything You gave me, attributing it to myself. How ugly is my sin: God humbles Himself and the creature exalts himself ... Forgive me, and teach me how to walk like You in humility, and acknowledge Your favor.

7.12.0.en: The Lord Christ moves the discourse here to the Pharisees, in a confrontation whose purpose is to expose their hypocrisy and the duplicity of their standards in judgment, and He also wants them to be witnesses against themselves in their transgressions of the Law for which they show zeal and for its ordinances. For Christ here lays bare to them that their relation to the Law is outward, while true knowledge and doing of the Law do not exist; for had they truly been subject to the Law by the Spirit of God, their thought would not have gone to killing Christ, and this is what Christ surprised them with, as One who knows the hidden things of their thoughts. But they denied what the Lord Christ exposed, and even added to their denial accusing Him of having a devil, adding to their hypocrisy and their thoughts a new sin, which is blasphemy against God Himself.

7.13.0.en: The work to which Christ refers is the miracle of healing the sick man of Bethesda (ch. 5), a miracle He performed on a Sabbath day, which provoked the anger of the Jews, and they regarded it as a breaking of the Sabbath, and a deed deserving death, and this verse is considered an introduction to (vv. 22-24).

7.14.0.en: In these verses the Lord Christ raises a logical case, through which He wants man's judgment to be just and logical, and not to go by the appearances of things. What the Lord wanted to offer as proof of this is the subject of circumcision. What Christ said was the following:

7.14.1.en: (1) Circumcision was a covenant, but from the days of the fathers, Abraham, and before the Law of Moses.

7.14.2.en: (2) The Law of Moses came forbidding any work on the Sabbath.

7.14.3.en: (3) But circumcision was on the eighth day after the male's birth, so if the eighth day came on the Sabbath, the Law permitted its performance.

7.14.4.en: (4) And the last question the Lord puts: if you break the Sabbath for circumcision, which could be postponed a day, and is a sign God asked of man, is the complete healing of a man and giving him the ability to move considered a breaking of the Sabbath? If God permitted breaking the Sabbath for circumcision, He permits breaking the Sabbath also for the life and good of man.

7.14.5.en: (5) Christ concludes His discourse (v. 24) with advice, not for the Jews only but for all of us, which is that man should not judge superficially and by appearance, but should fully understand the divine purpose.

7.14.6.en: For this reason, beloved, we find that the saints of the Church never hastened in their judgments, but examined everything in the fear of God and the understanding of the Holy Spirit, and all fled from condemning another ... For which of us knows enough to pass judgments on others?!

7.15.s.en: (3) The Jews' perplexity at Christ's words

7.15.0.en: "Them of Jerusalem": that is, the people of the city, and not the Jews who had come to it. They are more learned and more attached to the leaders, and know what they harbor toward the person of Christ. The people of Jerusalem fell into perplexity for the following reasons:

7.15.1.en: (1) That Christ speaks and teaches openly, and none of the leaders (the priests and Pharisees) interrupted Him or stopped Him. (2) Perhaps the reason was that the leaders themselves believed that He is the Christ, and for this reason did not oppose or resist Him, though they had decided earlier to kill Him.

7.15.2.en: (3) But what perplexed them most was a mistaken tradition and teaching that prevailed among the teachers of the Jews, that when the Christ comes, no one will know whence He comes, but He will appear suddenly in the temple; as for this man, despite His works, miracles and teachings, they know His origin, His family and His brethren.

7.16.0.en: "Then cried Jesus": that is, He raised His voice more than He had been teaching with, saying and answering them that what they know of Him is what the prophets testified, that the Christ is born in Bethlehem; and this is what the leaders answered Herod when he asked: "Where should Christ be born?" (Mt 2:4-5). But the Lord was not content with declaring that their bodily knowledge of Him agrees with His being the Christ, but added a theological dimension, which is that the One who sent Him is God the Father, the True One, whom, because of your literalism and your mistaken tradition, you have gone astray in knowing and in knowing His purpose. Consequently, as for my knowledge, I know Him, for I am from Him and from His essence and the same eternal divine nature, and He is the One who sent me (v. 29) as I have said many times before.

7.17.0.en: The Lord Christ's words provoked them, that they do not know God, they who regard themselves as His chosen people, so they tried to seize Him, but no one could, because God Himself did not allow them. And this is what St. John indicated: "because His hour was not yet come."

7.17.1.en: From this we learn two things:

7.17.2.en: The first: it concerns Christ, who said that He alone has the authority to lay down His life and take it again; and this is a confirmation of His divine power alone.

7.17.3.en: The second: it is a lesson for us all, that however much the wicked try to touch the children of God, they will be able to do nothing except what God permits ... For this reason we pray, in the Prayer of Thanksgiving and the Creed, calling our God, the protector of His Church, "the Almighty," an attribute that spreads reassurance and stability in the soul of the people, because all things are in the hand of God, the Lover of mankind.

7.18.0.en: "Many of the people believed on Him": that is, the simple folk, and not the rulers of the Jews, and they expressed their faith by a simple rhetorical question, directed to the leaders who rejected the Lord Jesus: "When Christ cometh, will he do more miracles than these which this man hath done?"

7.19.s.en: (4) Christ foretells His ascension and the working of the Holy Spirit

7.19.0.en: The Pharisees heard of the crowd's faith that He is the Christ, so they sent their servants to seize Him. The difference between this time and the previous one is that the first time it was individuals from the people who wanted to lay hold of Christ; but this time they are servants commissioned, by force of law, by the chief priests and the Pharisees, who together form the "Sanhedrin" council in Jerusalem, which consists of seventy of its elders, the leaders of the Jews, and so it is also called the Council of the Seventy; it is the supreme council to which all the subordinate councils belong. It is also the greatest Jewish authority that takes decisions in the religious affairs of the Jews, and many of the scribes were also members of this council; and it is the highest civil authority of the Jews after the Roman state.

7.20.0.en: The Lord Christ in His answer refers to the short time remaining for His ministry on earth, about six months, from the feast of tabernacles to the Passover, and after that He will be crucified and die, and rise, and ascend; and they will no longer find Him, for He will be in the bosom of His Father, the place from which He came down (ch. 1:18).

7.20.1.en: "Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me": this is also what the Lord said in (Lk 17:22): "The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man," and it means that those who reject Him now are the very ones who will regret His going and parting, after He declares the glory of Himself by His resurrection and ascension.

7.20.2.en: "Where I am": that is, while I am in all My glory, and in the bosom of My Father; no one who rejected the Son of Man and did not believe in Him will be able to enter the Holy of Holies, and enjoy eternal life with Him there, which was given only to everyone who believed in Him and acted on His word. And the speech in all its meaning is that although the servants were commissioned by force of law to seize Christ, He alone has the authority to determine this time, as before in (v. 30).

7.21.0.en: An addition to a scene recurring especially in the Gospel of St. John, which is that what the Lord Christ means, the people understand in another way ... All that came in (vv. 33, 34), some of those present interpreted as meaning that Christ, because of His failure to convince the Jews that He is the Christ, might go to the Greeks and teach the Jews of the Dispersion, that is, the Jews scattered and living in the land of the Greeks, trying to attract them, and make them believe in Him.

7.22.0.en: It shows the inner feelings of the Jews, which carry contempt and lack of understanding more than anything else.

7.23.0.en: "The last day": it is the eighth day (of the feast of tabernacles) and the greatest of them, because of the number of those celebrating, and because it is a day of retreat on which no work is done. There was a rite accompanying this feast which must be mentioned, because of its relation to what the Lord Christ will say in this verse ... This rite was that the high priest would go for 7 days and fill a golden jar with water from the pool of Siloam, and pour it on the bronze altar, and meanwhile all the people would sing all the prophecies concerning water, in remembrance of the water coming out of the rock in the wilderness, and the salvation of all the people ... throughout the seven days the souls are bound to the rock and to the water as a symbol of life ... And here came Christ's word on the eighth day about spiritual water, describing Himself as the true Rock, in place of the symbol in the wilderness, calling and inviting all to come and drink from Him, that they may have true life. And this is what the Lord also declared in the Book of Revelation, when He said: "And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely" (Rev 22:17).

7.23.1.en: Yes, beloved ... You are the only source of quenching, for all the allurements of the world are a mirage, but You are the only true spring, as Isaiah said of You: "like a spring of water, whose waters fail not" (Isa 58:11)."

7.23.2.en: For You are the Creator ... and consequently You are the One who knows the needs of the soul You created, and who is able to satisfy it, and all that is other than You is vanity, and a panting after desires that leave nothing but dryness ... So water me, O spring of love, with the water of Your love, and make me grow in Your grace working in me, renewing the vows of my baptism, O water of life.

7.24.0.en: The Lord returns and affirms that the source of every gift, grace and bestowal is faith in Him, and this is what St. John was committed to highlighting in his whole Gospel. And the gift of faith this time is the work of Christ by the Holy Spirit in the soul that believes in Him, so that it has the fruit of life, and an abundance of spiritual gifts; for Christ is the spring, and the soul that follows Him takes from Him, so that the spring of Christ in it becomes a current that does not stop ... see ch. 4:14 in His discourse with the Samaritan woman ...

7.24.1.en: And in (v. 39), St. John links faith in Christ with receiving the gift of the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in the name of Christ to all who believe in Him. He also refers here to future events which he himself lived through as well, namely that the Holy Spirit would not come upon the believers until after Christ's death, resurrection and ascension in glory.

7.24.2.en: It is noted that when the Church speaks of faith, she means practical faith, and not theoretical faith like the faith of the scribes and Pharisees, or even the faith of the demons (Jas 2:19), but as the Lord said: everyone who believes in Me and keeps My commandments ...

7.25.0.en: The opinions of the listeners differed into 3 opinions:

7.25.1.en: The first group: saw that He is the great Prophet of whom Moses foretold (Deut 18:15), but the Jews awaited Him for political salvation from the Romans, after a long period in which the scene was empty of great prophets, and they did not understand that He is the Savior from sin.

7.25.2.en: And the second group: saw that He is the Christ, through His miracles and His parables and His spiritual discourses, which did not resemble the discourses of all the teachers or the scribes and Pharisees ...

7.25.3.en: As for the third group: it denied this, and justified its denial on the ground that Jesus was known to them to be from Nazareth, whereas He is supposed to be from Bethlehem as in the Scriptures. Had this group investigated carefully, it would have known that Christ was in fact born in Bethlehem (Mt 2:1-6; see also Mic 5:2), though His upbringing was in Nazareth and Galilee of the Gentiles.

7.25.4.en: Our great God ... we often slip, and enter into inquiries and mazes which seem outwardly to be all about You, but this slipping takes us far from You, although You are the God of the simple, and Your gifts and bestowals remain as they are. So do not let us be occupied with what takes us away from life with You, for we are all like dry land longing for the spring of Your living water, and the gift of Your Holy Spirit, that our life may flourish in You and grow in Your Spirit.

7.26.0.en: As for the people who wanted to arrest Him, they are the servants of the chief priests (v. 32), and they will be spoken of.

7.26.1.en: (5) The rulers of the Jews reject Christ (vv. 45-53):

7.26.2.en: 45- "Then came the officers to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said unto them, Why have ye not brought him?"

7.26.3.en: 46- "The officers answered, Never man spake like this man. 47- Then answered them the Pharisees, Are ye also deceived? 48- Have any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed on him? 49- But this people who knoweth not the law are cursed. 50- Nicodemus saith unto them, (he that came to Jesus by night, being one of them,) 51- Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?"

7.26.4.en: 52- "They answered and said unto him, Art thou also of Galilee? Search, and look: for out of Galilee ariseth no prophet."

7.26.5.en: 53- "And every man went unto his own house."

7.27.0.en: The servants commissioned by the Sanhedrin (see v. 32) returned without arresting Christ, for the following reasons:

7.27.1.en: (1) Their personal being moved by Christ's teachings, the like of which they had not seen.

7.27.2.en: (2) The inclination of most of the people to Christ's side, whether regarding Him as the Prophet or the awaited Christ. And the witness these servants brought was a true witness of what they had seen, and its substance was that, were it not for their fear of the authority of the leaders, they would also have said that He is the Christ. We infer this from the sum of their witness: "words not of a man," that is, that He is not a man. And this faithful reply and strong witness provoked the rulers of the Jews, whose fury reached its limit, so that they accused the servants of going astray.

7.28.0.en: The speech here is on the tongue of the council of priests and Pharisees, the rulers, and it is a scornful rhetorical question, after hearing the servants' shameful and unexpected answer, and its meaning is that nothing remains except that one of us also believes in this deceiver. And as a kind of justification of what happened, they put the blame on this people, that they are an ignorant people, with no knowledge of the Law, a people easily deceived. And St. John reveals to us the hardness of heart of those who claimed to be shepherds and teachers, when they described their people and flock as a cursed people.

7.29.0.en: And the speech is to "Nicodemus," whom St. John presented to us before, in (ch. 3), in the night dialogue with Christ about Baptism, who acknowledged in his speech: "we know that thou art a teacher come from God" (ch. 3:2). Nicodemus combined faith in Christ with fear also of the rest of the leaders. For this reason we find him, in (v. 51), trying to defend Christ, and to reduce the spirit of revolt among the rest of the Pharisees and chief priests, by appealing for a lawful right by the force of the Law in favor of Christ, and this right is that the Law decrees that no man be judged without a trial, that is, in the language of law, that Christ is innocent until His guilt is proved.

7.30.0.en: The Pharisees' answer to Nicodemus was an evasion of the answer they owed to what he said, and, with a kind of mockery of him, departing from the objectivity of the dialogue, for they knew that he was not from Galilee. And this mocking accusation means: why do you favor this man as though you were from his birthplace? in an attempt to silence him, and justify their position, as they said to him: it was never recorded that a prophet came out of Galilee ...

7.30.1.en: It is noted that even this proof is wrong, for the prophet Jonah was from Galilee, and so were Hosea, Nahum, Elijah and Elisha, by lineage.

7.31.0.en: The end of the matter and the end of the feast of tabernacles was that each went to his house with feelings of rage and helplessness, because of the people gathering around Christ, and the servants' not obeying in arresting Him. In this way God fulfilled His purpose of His not being arrested, for His hour had not yet come.

7.31.1.en: She who was caught in adultery; faith in Christ
